quiz.q: Why does Hannah Arendt consider 'Action' the highest level of the Vita Activa?
options: It produces permanent physical objects that endure beyond individual biological existence.
It satisfies the basic biological survival necessities required by all living organisms.
It enables direct political participation among citizens, which alone provides complete human freedom.
It allows solitary philosophical contemplation and quiet reflection away from the public sphere.
quiz.why: Arendt argues that while labour meets biological needs and work fabricates objects, only collective political action secures genuine human freedom.

quiz.q: How does Hannah Arendt distinguish twentieth-century totalitarianism from traditional autocratic governance?
options: Totalitarian regimes make violence an end in itself, whereas traditional autocracies used violence as a means.
Totalitarian regimes depend on pre-modern religious myths, whereas traditional autocracies relied on advanced scientific technology.
Totalitarian regimes merely suppress public speech, whereas traditional autocracies systematically sought complete control over inner thought.
Totalitarian regimes originate from feudal agrarian disputes, whereas traditional autocracies developed strictly from industrial capitalist expansion.
quiz.why: Traditional autocracies used violence instrumentally to enforce obedience, whereas totalitarianism treats terror as an end in itself to control human souls.

quiz.q: According to Hannah Arendt's political theory, what is the defining characteristic of genuine power?
options: It represents an individual's sovereign ability to command others and force obedience through coercion.
It emerges spontaneously when citizens act together in concert and vanishes when they disperse.
It is permanently stored within official state apparatuses and exercised through bureaucratic dominance.
It derives primarily from the monopolistic control of economic capital and material resources.
quiz.why: Arendt defines power as a sui-generis phenomenon that arises when people cooperate in public and disappears once they return to private life.

quiz.q: What central conclusion did Hannah Arendt reach from observing Adolf Eichmann's trial in Jerusalem?
options: Totalitarian crimes are carried out exclusively by fanatical sadists driven by deep pathological hatred.
Strict adherence to administrative legal procedures guarantees moral integrity within modern bureaucratic governance.
Ideological atrocities cease entirely once civil service officials are granted greater individual discretion.
Extreme evil becomes banal when ordinary people commit horrific acts through an unthinking suspension of moral judgement.
quiz.why: Arendt observed that Eichmann acted not out of psychotic hatred, but through a thoughtless inability to reflect upon the moral consequences of his duties.
